# The Salt Between Words

The bottle washed up on a Tuesday, which was the day Elias permitted himself to feel sorry.

He'd been keeper of the Vell Point Light for eleven years, ever since Margot's lungs finally gave out and the world narrowed to the beam and the fog and the slow grinding of the gears. The lighthouse stood on a shelf of black rock three miles from the nearest village, and the only other human voice he heard for weeks at a time was his own, murmuring the log entries into the cold air. *Wind NW, 22 knots. Visibility four miles. Lamp serviced. No incidents.*

He found the bottle half-buried in the shingle below the gallery walk, its green glass fogged with salt and time. It wasn't sealed with wax. The cork had worked loose, and the paper inside was a pale, water-stained rectangle
